This paper uses explainable-AI techniques to generate grounded explanations for speech deepfake detection, powered by large language models working with audio, no extra training required. It targets audio-security researchers.
arxiv-2606-16237: Some math runs the clock back: dealt a last page, it replays the road that got there. This paper weighs such back-run dice rules with spread and jumps, nailing when answers live and how they stack up. For chance-math pros in banks and labs.
arxiv-2606-16737: Scientists check equations by units — meters, seconds, kilograms must line up. The Buckingham Pi theorem is the classic tool for that. arxiv-2606-16837: Voice fraud uses spoofed speech — cloned or synthesized voices. This paper detects spoofs robustly with temporal pyramid modeling: reading the audio at many time scales at once. It is for speech-security researchers fighting voice deepfakes. Many scales, fewer misses.
